analysis.title: AI Adoption Tracker: October 2026: Adoption Rises to 24.6%
key_insights: US firm AI adoption rose 0.8pp to 24.6% of establishments in the Census Bureau's BTOS survey. Firms expect adoption to reach 28.6% within the next 6 months.
Adoption is approaching 50% in the information, professional and finance sectors. Computing, securities and publishing firms lead at the subsector level.
Over half of establishments with 250+ employees expect to be using AI in the next six months.

The Census Bureau changed its question wording from AI use in 'producing goods and services' to 'any business functions' starting with the December 4, 2025 release. This caused a level shift, and GS tracks adoption under the new methodology.
Equity analysts expect global semiconductor revenue to reach $872bn (annualized) by end-2026. 2026 gross profit forecast revisions since 2022Q3 for AI-exposed global public companies stand at $1.1tn.
AI-related hardware investment in the US national accounts is $613bn above its 2022 level (3-month annualized average), equal to 1.9% of GDP.
AI-related hardware shipments from Taiwan are 88% above September 2022 levels. South Korea tech exports rose by $8.8bn to $56bn in September.
GS expects $82bn in global AI-related net exports from AI exporters in October (nowcast).

Employment drags persist in industries with established AI use cases (marketing, graphic design, customer service, some tech occupations). Data-center-exposed construction employment is up 315k since 2022 relative to broader construction trends.

Three-month averages in nonmanufacturing payrolls and unemployment show a statistically significant relationship with AI adoption at the subsector level. Higher adoption is associated with weaker job growth and higher unemployment. Effects on other labor market outcomes are not significant.

Average monthly job growth in AI-affected industries over the last 3 months is -6k. Tech's employment share continues to fall below its long-run trend, and unemployment among young tech workers has fallen back in line with all tech workers.

Corporate layoffs attributed to AI affected 4.0k employees in the latest month, bringing the total since May 2023 to 207k. 23% of Russell 3000 companies that have reported Q3 results mentioned AI and labor-related keywords on earnings calls.
Active AI-related job postings stand at 116k in the US, and the share of AI-related postings continues to rise across major developed markets.
Academic studies imply a 23% average productivity uplift from generative AI (median 20%). Company anecdotes imply about 32% (median 30%). Economy-wide impacts remain modest.

Industries with higher AI adoption show a slight acceleration in productivity growth over the past year in official US data. GS finds no relationship between company-level AI exposure and margin growth.

Business surveys show rising adoption but limited returns. Dun & Bradstreet finds 65% plan to raise AI spending but only 28% report broad or strong returns, and only 8% say their data is fully ready for AI at scale. Firms in Europe and Asia report the highest ROI rates.
earnings_insights: 23% of Russell 3000 companies that have reported Q3 2026 results so far mentioned AI and labor-related keywords in their earnings calls (GS Data Works).

Equity analysts expect global semiconductor revenue of $872bn (annualized) by end-2026, a forecast. 2026 gross profit forecast revisions since 2022Q3 for AI-exposed global public companies stand at $1.1tn.
GS finds no relationship between company-level AI exposure and margin growth (FactSet data).

risk_factors: Only 8% of businesses say their enterprise data is fully ready to support AI at scale, a potential hurdle for adoption and productivity returns (Dun & Bradstreet).
Economy-wide productivity gains remain modest despite large gains in the limited areas where generative AI is deployed.
AI adoption is associated with weaker job growth and higher unemployment in nonmanufacturing subsectors, with continued employment drags in tech and some white-collar occupations.
The Census question wording change in December 2025 created a level shift, which limits comparison with earlier history.

Exhibit 19 shows average monthly job growth in AI-affected industries over the last 3 months at -6k.
Exhibit 26 shows data-center-exposed construction employment up 315k since 2022 versus other construction employment trend.
Exhibit 28 shows academic study productivity gains with a median of 20% and an average of 23%. Exhibit 29 shows company anecdotes with a median of 30% and an average of 32%.

tension_points.bull_case: AI is lifting productivity. Academic studies imply a 23% average uplift and company anecdotes about 32%. Industries with higher adoption show slightly stronger productivity growth in official US data, and data-center construction employment is up 315k since 2022.
tension_points.bear_case: Higher adoption is associated with weaker job growth and higher unemployment at the subsector level (t-stats of -2.07 and 4.20). Employment growth in AI-affected industries is -6k per month, and AI-attributed layoffs total 207k since May 2023.

theme_stances.key_argument: Higher AI adoption at the subsector level is associated with weaker job growth and higher unemployment, with visible drags in specific industries.
theme_stances.evidence: higher adoption associated with weaker job growth and higher unemployment

theme_stances.key_argument: AI-related investment growth remains strong across semiconductors, US hardware investment and Asian tech exports.
theme_stances.evidence: AI-related investment growth remains strong, particularly for semiconductors

theme_stances.key_argument: Large productivity gains appear only in limited areas where generative AI is deployed, with modest economy-wide signs.
theme_stances.evidence: only modest signs of economy-wide impacts
